content.rendered:
Abide in Me, and I in you. The fruit does not come from the branch trying harder. It comes from the branch staying connected. Stay where you are loved.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, June 7, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit; apart from me you can do nothing.”
John 15:5 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Jesus is on the way to the cross when He says this. It is the night before His crucifixion. He has just shared the Passover meal with His friends. He has washed their feet. He has told them He is going to prepare a place for them. And then, with His arrest only hours away, He takes them to one of the most patient, slow-paced agricultural metaphors in all of Scripture. He talks about a vine, branches and fruit.

The lesson He wants them to carry into the next forty-eight hours, when His body is in a tomb and everything they have hoped for seems to have ended, is one word in Greek: meinate. Abide. Remain. Stay. Continue. He repeats it ten times in this short chapter. Whatever else they forget, Jesus does not want them to forget this. The Christian life is not primarily activity. It is connection. The branch does not produce fruit by working harder. The branch produces fruit by staying attached to the vine.

This is a profoundly freeing word for striving believers. Apart from Me you can do nothing, Jesus says. Not little. Not less than your potential. Nothing. The most disciplined Christian, with the best devotional habits and the strongest theological library, produces nothing of eternal value when disconnected from Jesus Himself. And the weakest believer, with no platform, no following, no obvious ministry, produces real fruit simply by abiding in Him.

Abiding is not mystical. It is just staying. Staying in prayer when prayer feels dry. Staying in His word when the page feels heavy. Staying in worship when the song does not move you. Staying in community when relationships are hard. Staying in obedience when the path is unclear. The Christian life is, at its most fundamental level, the discipline of not leaving Jesus when staying becomes inconvenient. The fruit grows from there.

Today, you are not asked to produce. You are asked to remain. The Spirit will produce what the Spirit produces, in a branch that simply will not let go of the vine.

Prayer

Lord Jesus, I abide in You today. I am not striving to produce. I am only staying. Hold me close to Yourself. When the day pulls at me, when the noise increases, when the distractions come, anchor me back to the One who is the vine. Let whatever fruit comes from this day be fruit that grew because I stayed where I was loved. In Your name. Amen.

Declaration

I abide in Christ, and Christ abides in me. I am not a branch trying to produce on my own. I am a branch staying connected to the vine. The life of Jesus flows through me. The fruit of the Spirit grows in me. I remain in Him today.
